# macOS shell (SwiftUI + AppKit) — **not implemented**

Status: **planned**. There is deliberately no Swift source here yet.

## Why there is no code in this directory

Writing an unverifiable shell would be worse than writing none:

* the development machine has no Swift toolchain, so nothing here could be
  compiled — the repository would carry a file that looks finished and has never
  been built;
* a correct client needs Swift protobuf stubs generated by
  `protoc-gen-swift` + `protoc-gen-grpc-swift` from `proto/*.proto`; without
  those, any Swift file would either not compile or would fake the wire format;
* spec rule 4 forbids shipping something that looks supported but is not.

The Windows shell is implemented and tested against the real core; the Linux
shell is written against the real gtk4-rs API but also unverified. macOS is the
one platform with neither, so it is marked planned and tracked in
`docs/architecture/task-status.md`.

## What implementing it requires

1. A macOS machine or CI runner (GitHub Actions `macos-latest`) with Xcode.
2. `protoc-gen-swift` and `protoc-gen-grpc-swift` on `PATH`, wired into a
   `scripts/generate-swift-protos.sh` that mirrors
   `scripts/generate-csharp-protos.ps1` (generate into `Sources/GgufShell/Generated`,
   commit, and let CI fail on drift).
3. A `Package.swift` depending on `grpc-swift` and the generated target.
4. `CoreBridge`: connect over the Unix socket at
   `~/Library/Application Support/GGUF AI Engine/run/core.sock` and call
   `UiService/GetSnapshot` — the same call the Windows shell makes.
5. SwiftUI views for Overview and Settings that render exactly the snapshot
   fields: tiles, feature rows (with status text and reason), settings groups and
   issues. No formatting or severity logic in Swift.
6. Tests mirroring `GgufAiEngine.Shell.Core.Tests`: endpoint derivation against
   the shared FNV-1a vectors, snapshot mapping, and one end-to-end test against
   the real `gguf-core` binary on the socket.

## Design decisions already fixed for it

- **Unified memory is not VRAM.** macOS reports memory topology, and the GPU page
  must not claim a discrete VRAM figure (spec §5.2).
- **Metal is the only backend.** CUDA/ROCm entries are shown as unsupported on
  this platform rather than hidden.
- **Endpoint is per data root**, same rule as Windows: `run/core.sock` inside the
  data root, so two installations never collide.
